string: 能跟我说说你的店吗？

original: Well - I've mostly been selling blades, arrows and traveling gear. Some I crafted, the others I bought from other artisans.
string: 嗯——我主要卖刀剑、箭矢和旅行装备。有些是我自己打造的，有些是从其他工匠那里买来的。

original: There are quite a few customers who keep returning, so business is good.
string: 有不少回头客，所以生意还不错。

original: Do you know why?
string: 你知道为什么吗？

original: Let's just say my customers always get what they need in my store, as long as it concerns the art of death.
string: 这么说吧——只要关乎死亡的艺术，我的顾客总能在我的店里找到他们需要的东西。

original: I spent years as a sellsword in all manners of warfare, and I know what serves me best in any situation.
string: 我当了多年的雇佣兵，经历过各种战事，我知道在任何情况下什么最适合自己。

original: What I sell is not just weapon, but also decades of wisdom.
string: 我卖的不仅仅是武器，还有几十年的智慧。

original: Do you like running a store, instead of being a sellsword?
string: 你喜欢开店胜过当雇佣兵吗？

original: Well, if I could, of course I prefer making art myself.
string: 嗯，如果可以的话，我当然更愿意亲手创造艺术。

original: But since you need me to stay at home, helping others make art will have to suffice.
string: 但既然你需要我留在家里，帮别人创造艺术也只好将就了。

original: Let's talk about something else.
string: 我们聊点别的吧。

original: A death cult rules this tomb. We should silence them forever.
string: 死灵教派统治着这座墓穴。我们应该让他们永远安静。

original: These necromancers toy with Death... They'll soon meet that which they think they master.
string: 这些死灵法师在玩弄死亡……他们很快就会与自认为掌控的东西面对面了。

original: I wonder what drove that necromancer down this path. The Redguards hate the undead even more so than my kind.
string: 我在想是什么驱使那个死灵法师走上这条路。红卫人比我们丹莫更憎恨亡灵。

original: I can understand the Redguard necromancer. She'd bring down those who watched condescendingly as her beloved died.
string: 我能理解那个红卫死灵法师。她要毁掉那些居高临下看着她爱人死去的人。

original: The necromancer's vengeance might be righteous, but her means had led to nothing but death... Let's leave this tomb behind.
string: 死灵法师的复仇或许是正义的，但她的手段带来的只有死亡……我们离开这座墓穴吧。

original: It seems the Redoran Guards are crumbling to the Ash Spawn attacks. Raven Rock won't be the first city to be buried in ash, nor will it be the last.
string: 看来瑞多然卫兵在灰烬怪的攻击下节节败退。鸦石镇不会是第一个被灰烬掩埋的城市，也不会是最后一个。

original: These "Ash Spawn" are unlike anything I've seen back on the mainland. I suspect dark arts are involved in their creation.
string: 这些"灰烬怪"跟我在大陆上见过的任何东西都不一样。我怀疑它们的诞生涉及黑暗法术。

original: I've seen the Imperials use criminals and Daedra, even undead when they're desperate - but an army of ashen monsters just might be the first.
string: 我见过帝国在绝望时使用罪犯、迪德拉，甚至亡灵——但一支灰烬怪物组成的大军，还真算是头一回。

original: I wonder what preserved the Imperial General's body. For how long he had died, he didn't look rotten at all.
string: 我在想是什么保存了那位帝国将军的尸体。死了那么久，他看起来竟然完全没有腐烂。

original: Considering we just saved Raven Rock from certain destruction, the Captain should've been more generous. They make do with what they can, I suppose.
string: 考虑到我们刚刚拯救了鸦石镇，让它免于毁灭，那个队长本该更慷慨一些的。不过……我想他们也只能给出这么多了。

original: You've done well killing that bandit back there. No one will mourn for thugs like her.
string: 干得漂亮，杀了那个强盗。没会人会为那种暴徒哀悼的。

original: This crypt gives me a strange unease. The bandits aren't the only things that dwell here.
string: 这座墓穴让我感到一种异样的不安。住在这里的可不只有那些强盗。

original: I would've cut down that bandit back there if it were up to me. Fools like her are just a waste of clean air.
string: 要我说，刚才那个强盗我早就砍了。她那种蠢货，连喘气都是在浪费干净的空气。

original: I see doubt and mutiny beset these bandits. We'll be wise to use that.
string: 这些强盗里头猜忌和叛意丛生。我们最好利用这一点。

original: I shed no tears for those bandits, but ordeals like the Pale Lady are precisely why I loathe dealing with the dead.
string: 我不会为那些强盗掉一滴泪，但像苍白夫人这种劫难——正是我厌恶跟死人打交道的理由。

original: That Altmer looks as if he'll cough his lungs out any moment. Will he even be alive to pay you when we get back?
string: 那个傲特莫看起来随时都会把肺咳出来。等我们回去的时候，他还能活着付你钱吗？

original: I see the White Phial is nothing but a few fragments. Well, that's not our problem - let's get back to the Altmer for our payment.
string: 看来白瓶只剩下几块碎片了。好吧，那不是我们的问题——回去找那个傲特莫拿报酬吧。

original: This Altmer is why I never take jobs from bedridden wretches. The dead pay no debts, and they know that all too well.
string: 这个傲特莫就是为什么我从不接卧病在床的可怜虫的活。死人付不了债——他们自己最清楚这一点。

original: I wonder if the White Phial can truly be repaired. Either way, I'll settle for the Phial or a fat purse of gold.
string: 我在想白瓶是否真的能修复。不管怎样，拿到白瓶或者一大袋金币，我都能接受。

original: So, the White Phial is restored after all. Had the young alchemist failed to do so, I suppose this shop would need a new name.
string: 看来白瓶终究还是修复了。如果那个年轻的炼金术士失败了——我想这家店得换个名字了。

original: Having seen how the Rieklings stained this mead hall, I'll never trust anything brewed here - Nord reclamation or not.
string: 见识了那些瑞克灵怎么糟蹋这个蜜酒厅之后，——不管诺德人收不收复，这地方酿的东西我绝不会碰。

original: That woman actually believed she stood a chance. What a fool.
string: 那个女人居然以为自己有机会。真是个蠢货。

original: People will say anything to excuse their failings. No matter - their payment is what counts.
string: 人们为了给自己的失败开脱，什么话都说得出来。无所谓——他们付的钱才是要紧的。

original: I've heard of the Red Eagle when I fought the Forsworn. They would scream his name in battle, as if it'd give them some divine protection.
string: 我跟弃誓者战斗时听说过红鹰。他们会在战场上尖叫他的名字，仿佛那能给他们带来某种神灵庇佑。

original: I heard the Red Eagle fought fiercely against Nord aggression. All that zeal turned out to be for naught after all.
string: 我听说红鹰曾激烈抵抗诺德人的侵略。到头来，那股狂热终究成了一场空。

original: We Dunmer have the Nerevarine. I suppose the Reachmen can have their Red Eagle.
string: 我们丹莫有尼瑞瓦因。弃誓者有个红鹰也正常。

original: All that's left of the Red Eagle are his sword and his title. Not his bloodline, not even his name. I suppose that's the fate of most heroes.
string: 红鹰留下的只有他的剑和他的名号。没有他的血脉，甚至没有他的真名。我想这就是大多数英雄的命运吧。

original: The Red Eagle is gone, and you're free to kill Nords and Forsworn alike with his sword. I suppose that's not the legacy he hoped for.
string: 红鹰已经消逝了，而你可以用他的剑随意杀戮诺德人和弃誓者。我猜，那应该不是他想要的传承。

original: There used to be a few Skooma cartels in Morrowind. I suppose the ash storms made for good cover for their operations.
string: 晨风以前也有几个斯库玛贩子团伙。我猜那些灰烬风暴正好帮他们打了掩护。

original: I've never taken Skooma myself. The stuff is poison for the mind.
string: 我自己从不碰斯库玛。那东西就是心智的毒药。

original: Riften will be Riften, with or without the Skooma cartel.
string: 裂谷城就那样，有没有斯库玛贩子都一样。

original: I don't know if it's the wolves, the Skooma, or just the cave itself - but it stinks worse than a mine full of sulfur.
string: 我不知道是那些狼、那些斯库玛、还是这洞本身——反正比硫磺矿还臭。

original: The cartel is gone, and a new one will soon swoop in and claim their place - Riften will always be Riften.
string: 贩子没了，很快又有新的扑进来占了他们的窝——裂谷城永远是裂谷城。

original: I've killed Hagravens before. Those witches always talk in honeyed lies before placing you on the altar. Let's stay guarded around this Illia.
string: 我以前杀过乌鸦鬼婆。那些巫婆嘴上说得好听，回头就把你送上祭坛。对这个伊雅，咱们还是留个心眼。

original: Illia seems all innocent and trusting, but I promise you - no pure soul would call this tower her home.
string: 伊雅看着天真又信任人，但我跟你保证——没有一个干净的灵魂会把这座塔叫作自己的家。

original: At this point, Illia has killed more witches than necessary to win your trust. Either she's true to her words, or she's a better schemer than I know.
string: 到了这一步，伊雅杀的女巫已经远远超过赢取你信任所需了。要么她说的句句属实——要么她就是我见过最会演戏的。

original: I see I misjudged Illia when I first saw her. She truly intended to do the right thing.
string: 看来我第一眼见到伊雅时看走眼了。她是真心想做正确的事。

original: So, the Steward dismissed the peasant's concerns about Wolfskull Cave. Once again, it's up to us to do the dirty work.
string: 所以，总管根本没把那农民对狼头骨洞穴的担忧当回事。又轮到我们来干脏活了。

original: Do you feel it too? There's an ominous chill in these ruins, whispering of terrors from ages past.
string: 你也感觉到了吧？这遗迹里有股不祥的寒意，低语着来自远古的恐惧。

original: Necromancers and their foul art, always the source of troubles. The peasant was right all along.
string: 死灵法师和他们那肮脏的勾当，永远是祸根。那个农民一直是对的。

original: So, that's what those necromancers were after - a dead Septim queen who ruled over the dead... And she is now free, all because of their folly.
string: 原来如此，那些死灵法师想要的是——一个死了的塞普汀女王，一个统治死者的女王……就因为他们的愚蠢，现在她自由了。

original: The Septim queen was bound to return after her escape. Living or dead, their kind are always too proud to stay silent.
string: 塞普汀女王逃出来之后必然会卷土重来。不管活的死的，他们那种人永远骄傲到不肯闭嘴。

original: Do you hear the dead's whispers? They're warning us away. Maybe it's the Septim queen's mind trick, cast out of fear.
string: 你听到死者的低语了吗？他们在警告我们离开。也许是塞普汀女王出于恐惧施展的把戏。

original: Vampires and walking corpses. Is that all the undead queen can muster?
string: 吸血鬼和行尸。那个不死女王就拿得出这点东西？

original: I grew weary of the Wolf Queen's voice. The dead should stay silent... Let's make it so again.
string: 我听够了狼女王的声音。死者就该沉默……让我们让她重新闭嘴吧。

original: The whispers have ceased. As I predicted, it was the Wolf Queen's trick. She feared us... even if she acted all mighty and terrible.
string: 低语声停了。不出我所料，是狼女王的把戏。她怕我们……尽管她装得一副不可一世的样子。

original: You'd think the Steward would be more generous to the vanquishers of Solitude's worst villain. I hope the catacomb's loot was good, at least.
string: 你可能会觉得，总管对消灭了独孤城最凶恶反派的功臣，会出手大方些。至少希望地下墓穴里的战利品还不错。

original: A house burned right in the middle of the town, and no one does anything about it - as if it's nothing out of the ordinary.
string: 镇子正中央一座房子烧了，没一个人管——好像这根本不算什么怪事。

original: With all the terrors that lurk in the marsh, the peasants chose to fight a simple wizard, of all things. That's Skyrim for you.
string: 沼泽里藏着那么多可怕的东西，结果那些农民偏偏挑一个普普通通的巫师来对付。这就是天际。

original: Playing hide and seek with a ghost is hardly a fair game - unless she wants to be found.
string: 跟一个鬼魂玩捉迷藏，这游戏本来就不公平——除非她自己想让你找到。

original: The truth of Morthal's terror is unveiled at last. Maybe the town can be saved after all.
string: 莫萨尔恐怖的真相终于揭开了。也许这镇子还有救。

original: The vampires are destroyed, but the air grows thickened with death. I wonder if we've truly quelled the evil, or only removed its competition.
string: 吸血鬼被灭了，但空气里的死气越来越重。我在想——我们是真的平息了邪恶，还是只是替它清掉了竞争对手。

original: So I guessed correctly. A Nord ruin slumbers beneath Raven Rock's mine. Now, let's see if it's as horrifying as the East Empire Company believed.
string: 果然让我猜中了。鸦石镇矿场下面沉睡着一座诺德遗迹。现在，让我们看看它是不是真像东帝国公司以为的那么可怕。

original: A skeleton, dead for centuries. No doubt, that's the old Imperial's great-grandfather.
string: 一具死了几百年的骷髅。没跑，就是那个老帝国人的曾祖父。

original: Here we are... the true secret of Raven Rock's mine. The source of all the terror in this ruin.
string: 到了……鸦石镇矿场真正的秘密。这座遗迹里所有恐惧的源头。

original: It has been a remarkable journey, but I long for the blue sky already. Well, no blue sky on Solstheim, perhaps, but any sky would be an improvement.
string: 这趟旅程确实不一般，但我已经开始想念蓝天了。好吧，索瑟海姆也许没有蓝天——但只要是天空，就是种改善。

original: Finally! Breathable air without the stench of the centuries-dead.
string: 终于！能喘口气了，没有那些陈年尸臭。

original: To be so naive that he'd deal with Maven Black-Briar's failure of an offspring? Maybe Louis deserves to eat his loss.
string: 天真到去跟玛雯·黑棘那个废物儿子做交易？路易士亏了也是活该。

original: If I ever had a son like Sibbi Black-Briar, I'd put him on a boat to Atmora and never look back.
string: 要是我有个儿子像西比·黑棘那样——我直接把他扔上去阿特莫拉的船，头也不回。

original: I almost pity Maven Black-Briar. For all her power and schemes, she stands to lose her empire to an offspring like Sibbi.
string: 我几乎有点可怜玛雯·黑棘了。她费尽心机爬到今天，结果自己的帝国可能毁在西比这种后代手里。

original: Good move telling that Breton's scheme to Maven Black-Briar. She would've found out anyway... No reason to put ourselves at risk for a corpse.
string: 把那个布莱顿人的阴谋告诉玛雯·黑棘——这步走得对。她迟早也会发现的……没必要为一具死尸把我们自己搭进去。

original: All this drama over a horse, and it's not even that handsome a steed. What a disappointment.
string: 闹出这么多破事就为一匹马，而且那匹马也算不上多好看。真让人失望。

original: Bear hunting isn't what I expected to be a vampire hunter's task.
string: 猎熊可不是我预想中吸血鬼猎人该干的活。

original: I suggest we simply head to the nearest Dwemer ruin for her gyro. No point wasting time on a wild chase amidst all this mud.
string: 我建议我们直接去最近的锻莫遗迹找她的陀螺仪。在这片烂泥地里瞎追纯属浪费时间。

original: So, we have ourselves a Dwemer expert. Slaughtering vampires with their steel just might elevate my art.
string: 看来我们找到了一位锻莫专家。用他们的钢铁来屠杀吸血鬼——说不定能提升我的艺术。

original: Seems to me Isran never even liked these 'old friends' of his. Such unifying force he'll make for.
string: 我看伊士冉压根就不喜欢他这些'老友'。他可真能团结人啊。

original: I wonder what this Florentius is capable of. Priest of Arkay? What is he going to do - exorcise the vampires? Or pray for their souls?
string: 我倒想知道这个佛伦提乌斯有多大本事。阿尔凯的祭司？他打算怎么着——给吸血鬼驱魔？还是为他们的灵魂祈祷？

original: Does Florentius... 'talk' to his god? Now I see why the people had that hesitant tone when they asked you to find him.
string: 佛伦提乌斯……能跟他的神'说话'？现在我明白那些人请你去找他的时候，为什么语气那么犹豫了。

original: Two elves who kidnapped a blacksmith? They're either from Raven Rock or the Thalmor - and I assure you, my people have no interest in Nord armor.
string: 两个精灵绑架了一个铁匠？要么是鸦石镇来的，要么是梭默——我跟你保证，我族人对诺德盔甲可没兴趣。

original: I thought this isle would be the last place to interest a Thalmor. Surely, there are greener pastures to conquer or plunder.
string: 我以为这座岛是梭默最不可能感兴趣的地方。肯定有更好的地方值得他们征服或掠夺吧。

original: I wonder what magic this 'Stalhrim' contains, so powerful that it made the Thalmor come all this way from Alinor.
string: 我在想这'魔冰'里到底有什么魔力，能让梭默从艾琳诺千里迢迢赶来。

original: I never expected that we'd do business with the Thalmor, but whoever pays well, I suppose.
string: 我没想到有一天我们居然会和梭默做交易——不过，谁出价高就跟谁做，我想是这样。

original: I've started to imagine how a Thalmor would look in Stalhrim armor. A blue Altmer would look like quite the spectacle, don't you think?
string: 我开始想象一个梭默穿上魔冰盔甲会是什么样子了。蓝皮肤的傲特莫——那场面一定很壮观，你不觉得吗？

original: It's not my first time escorting a historian through an old ruin, though my first was inconceivably more talkative... and annoying.
string: 这不是我第一次护送历史学家逛遗迹了。不过上一个话多得吓人……而且烦人。

original: The Empire built fortresses like this to last. Considering its age, it still holds up well.
string: 帝国建造的堡垒就是这样经久耐用。以它的年代来看，它仍然保存得很好。

original: I could get used to this place. The darkness gives me a warm comfort.
string: 我能习惯这个地方。黑暗给我一种温暖的慰藉。

original: With the wars and the debts, the Jarls and the generals have gradually lost control of their forts.
string: 由于战争和债务，领主们和将军们渐渐失去了对堡垒的控制。

original: Imperial forts like this used to dot the landscapes of Morrowind. After the Red Year, they've mostly crumbled into dust.
string: 像这样的帝国堡垒曾经遍布晨风的大地。红年之后，它们大多已经化为尘土了。

original: I once wiped out a fortress in a single night. Poisoned wine does the trick every time - that, and my silent steps.
string: 我曾经一夜之间灭掉了一座堡垒。毒酒每次都管用——再加上我无声的步伐。

original: Solitude is one of the few Skyrim cities that agree with me.
string: 独孤城是少数几个让我觉得合拍的天际城市之一。

original: Solitude values real art, yet it's never lacking in schemes and shadows. This just might be the perfect city for someone like me.
string: 独孤城珍视真正的艺术，但这里的阴谋和暗影也从来不缺。这或许正是适合我这样的人的城市。

original: I may enjoy Nord mead, but Solitude's fine wine is unlike any other.
string: 我或许喜欢喝诺德蜜酒，但独孤城的精品葡萄酒别具一格。

original: Adara and I used to play with the instruments at the day's end. So many fond memories we had with the flutes...
string: 阿达拉和我以前常在一天结束时演奏乐器。我们用那些笛子留下了那么多美好的回忆……

original: Maybe we can play with the flute later, like I used to with Adara.
string: 也许我们待会可以吹吹笛子，就像我以前和阿达拉那样。

original: One can make such great art with a flute.
string: 一支笛子也能创造出如此伟大的艺术。

original: I wonder if the dragons feel fear. That must be the only thing they know when you devour their souls.
string: 我在想龙会不会感到恐惧。当你吞噬它们的灵魂时，那一定就是它们唯一能感受到的东西。

original: I've been struck by the soul trap spell a few times. When you absorb the dragons' souls, I can only imagine they feel the agony tenfold.
string: 我被摄魂陷阱击中过几次。当你吸收龙魂的时候，我只能想象它们承受的痛苦是你的十倍。

original: So, the dragon god made you to kill his children and eat their souls? I've seen worse parents.
string: 所以，龙神造出你就是为了杀死他的孩子，吃掉他们的灵魂？我见过更差劲的父母。

original: If you think the dragons are irritating, then you don't know the cliff racers. Those nasty critters never have the decency to stay grounded.
string: 如果你觉得龙很烦人，那是你没见识过峭壁行者。那些讨厌的东西从来不懂得待在地上。

original: The dragons breathe magic as effortlessly as we spit. It would be wise to take precautions against their ice or fire.
string: 龙吐息魔法就像我们吐口水一样轻松。最好做好防范，抵御它们的冰霜或火焰。

original: I suppose this place can't get any filthier... Bathing time can't come soon enough.
string: 我想这个地方不会再更脏了……真想赶紧洗个澡。

original: The longer we stay here, the more we smell like this place's denizens. I suggest we find the nearest pond soon as we leave this accursed place.
string: 我们在这里待得越久，身上的味道就越像这里的居民。我建议一离开这个该死的地方就去找最近的水塘。

original: A thorough bath always does us adventuring type wonders.
string: 好好洗个澡，对我们这些冒险者来说总是有奇效。

original: Why don't we have a long, warm bath - just you and me, undisturbed by anything.
string: 我们何不洗个长长的热水澡——就你和我，不受任何打扰。

original: We have a long road ahead. A quick bath in a nearby pond ought to refresh our spirits... Not to mention it'll get rid of the odor.
string: 前路漫漫。在附近的水塘里快速洗个澡，应该能让我们的精神振作起来……更别说还能去掉身上的臭味。

original: But no matter. Soon as our contract is over, the Stormcloaks will see their patrols disappear without a trace.
string: 不过无所谓了。等合同一结束，风暴斗篷就会发现他们的巡逻队消失得无影无踪。

original: I tolerate the Stormcloaks because of you, my love - but had it not been for you, I'd see their patrols slaughtered in the dark.
string: 我容忍风暴斗篷是因为你，我的爱人——但若不是因为你，我早就看着他们的巡逻队在暗处被屠戮殆尽了。

original: What do you think about Raven Rock's assassination plot?
string: 你对鸦石镇的刺杀阴谋怎么看？

original: Assassination, family feuds, backstabbing - these are all parts of a Dunmer noble's daily life.
string: 刺杀、家族世仇、背后捅刀——这都是丹莫贵族日常生活的一部分。

original: I don't know which side is more right in this situation - the Redoran or the Ulen. But knowing Morrowind, the answer is most certainly neither.
string: 我不知道在这种情况下哪一方更正确——是瑞多然还是乌伦。但以我对晨风的了解，答案肯定两方都不是。

original: But no matter. Point your blade at the Ulen, and I'll wipe them out as you desire.
string: 不过无所谓。只要你把剑指向乌伦，我就按你的意愿把他们清除干净。

original: Why is neither side right?
string: 为什么两边都不对？

original: The Great Houses feud over lands, gold and ancestral claims. The conflict between the Redoran and the Ulen was no different, whatever they may say.
string: 大家族之间的世仇无非是为了土地、金币和祖先宣称权。瑞多然和乌伦之间的冲突也不例外，不管他们怎么说。

original: Of course, the Redoran can make all their claims about their righteous purge of House Hlaalu. The dead cannot talk back after all.
string: 当然，瑞多然可以大谈他们如何正义地清算了哈拉鲁家族。毕竟死人不会反驳。

original: It seems you're no stranger to Great House politics.
string: 看来你对大家族的政治并不陌生。

original: In my childhood, I'd occasionally play the inconspicuous urchin for Great House schemers.
string: 小时候，我偶尔会为那些大家族阴谋家扮演不起眼的小乞丐。

original: While I poured their Matze, those gluttonous nobles would announce their grand plot to their allies, only for me to trade it for a warm meal.
string: 当我在倒玛兹的时候，那些饕餮贵族会向盟友宣布他们的宏伟计划——而我则拿这些情报换一顿热饭。

original: It's almost pitiful how no one ever suspected a drink pourer, just because she seemed all harmless and small.
string: 从来没有人怀疑过一个倒酒的，就因为她看起来人畜无害、身材矮小——这几乎让人觉得可怜。

original: That's dishonorable.
string: 那可不光彩。

original: In contrast to those who literally plotted to murder my employers for power?
string: 跟那些为了权力而密谋谋杀我雇主的人比起来？

original: Honor is only a fancy garment afforded by those who live in peace.
string: 荣誉不过是只有生活在和平中的人才穿得起的一件华丽外衣。

original: A meal in exchange of political advantage? Sounds like a bargain.
string: 一顿饭换一个政治优势？听起来挺划算的。

original: They needed their advantage, and I needed my belly to stop drumming. All things considered, we both got what we wanted.
string: 他们需要他们的优势，而我要让自己的肚子不再咕咕叫。总的来说，我们都得到了想要的。

original: But of course, my loyalty is much more expensive than porridge and meat nowadays.
string: 当然，如今我的忠诚，可比一碗粥和肉贵得多了。

original: So you've adapted to the shadows since your childhood.
string: 所以你从小就已经适应了暗影。

original: I guess this life chose me as much as I chose it.
string: 我想，与其说我选择了这种生活，不如说它选择了我。

original: Honestly, these Dunmeri intrigues are too messy for my liking.
string: 老实说，这些丹莫的阴谋太混乱了，我不喜欢。

original: And I won't blame you for it... Our society is as complex as a maze to most, with each exit leading only to another labyrinth.
string: 我也不会因此责怪你……我们的社会对大多数人来说就像一座迷宫，每个出口通向的只是另一座迷宫。

original: Well, you did resolve the Silver-Blood situation in Markarth, did you not? I say this is child's play compared to that.
string: 但是，你不是解决了马卡斯城银血家族的事吗？跟那件事比起来，这不过是小儿科。

original: In any event, you accepted a contract from the Councilor. It's only fair that you complete his task, or let him know your wish.
string: 无论如何，你接受了议员的合同。完成他的任务，或者让他知道你的意愿——这才公平。

original: Let's find out those Ulen and finish them.
string: 去找到那些乌伦家族的家伙，干掉他们。

original: As you say.
string: 听你的。

original: But the Ulen are a threat to Raven Rock's peace.
string: 但乌伦家族对鸦石镇的和平构成了威胁。

original: A threat to the Redoran's peace. Had it been the Ulen who ruled Raven Rock, the Redoran would've attempted the same.
string: 是对瑞多然家族的和平的威胁。如果是乌伦家族统治鸦石镇，瑞多然也会做同样的事。

original: Different names, same plots. Such is the long saga of my people.
string: 不同的名号，同样的阴谋。这就是我族人漫长的编年史。

original: The victor wrote the history.
string: 历史是胜利者书写的。

original: And that's the truth.
string: 事实正是如此。

original: If you're employed by the East Empire Company, how can you still work for me?
string: 你既然受雇于东帝国公司，怎么还能为我工作？

original: To answer it simply, they don't require my service every moment.
string: 简单说——他们不是时时刻刻都需要我。

original: I'm free to pursue other work while they have no need for me. The more contracts I complete, the sooner I can repay this debt.
string: 他们用不着我的时候，我可以自由接别的活。我完成的合同越多，就能越早还清这笔债。

original: But where they need my service, I'll be obligated to abandon all other work to serve their interests. Such are the terms of their 'offer'.
string: 但只要他们需要我，我就有义务放下所有其他工作，为他们办事。这就是他们那个'提议'的条款。

original: That sounds only fair.
string: 听起来还算公平。

original: Fair to the Company, as always.
string: 对公司公平罢了——一向如此。

original: Do they pay you when they don't need you?
string: 他们不用你的时候，也付你钱吗？

original: If you wouldn't pay for a mead you didn't drink, then why would they pay for a service they didn't use?
string: 你不会为没喝的蜜酒付钱——那他们为什么要为没用的服务付钱？

original: That sounds harsh.
string: 听起来真够苛刻的。

original: When an Imperial sets the terms, they've already calculated all their gains and losses.
string: 帝国人定条件的时候，早就把自己的得失都算得一清二楚了。

original: Wait, what will happen to us if they summon you now?
string: 等等，要是他们现在把你召回去，我们怎么办？

original: Then I'll have no choice but to return to their service until their need for me expires. Unless you wish to come along, that is.
string: 那我就只能回去，直到他们不再需要我为止。当然——除非你愿意一起来。

original: If not... I suppose the least I could do is to give you a refund.
string: 如果不来的话……我想我至少还能把钱退给你。

original: Why are you giving me that look, Jenassa?
string: 你为什么那样看着我，简拉萨？

original: It's nothing.
string: 没什么。

original: No, I can tell something's on your mind. You looked just like Faida when she lost my brother.
string: 不，我看得出来你有心事。你刚才的表情，就像菲达失去我哥哥时那样。

original: Well, I... You look like someone from my past, is all.
string: 嗯，我……你看起来像我过去认识的一个人，就这个。

original: Ah, I'd say I could be that person, but I'm certain I'd remember you. After all, you leave quite the impression on everyone you meet.
string: 啊，我倒想说我可能就是那个人——但我肯定我会记得你。毕竟，你给每个见过你的人都留下了深刻的印象。

original: No, you can't possibly be her... She died thirty years ago.
string: 不，你不可能是她……她三十年前就死了。

original: Jenassa, you mentioned I looked like someone from your past... who died thirty years ago? Who was that?
string: 简拉萨，你说我看起来像你过去认识的一个人……三十年前就死了？那是谁？

original: She was my first love in Skyrim. The one who taught me that warmth exists even in the frozen north.
string: 她是我在天际的第一个爱人。是她教会我——即使在冰封的北方，也有温暖存在。

original: Oh. I didn't realize she was your... I mean, my condolences.
string: 哦。我不知道她是你……我是说，请节哀。

original: Thank you.
string: 谢谢。

original: She was a bard - the most gifted of her class. When we were together, she'd always perform the world's most beautiful art for me.
string: 她是个诗人——那是她那一行里最有天分的人。我们在一起的时候，她总是为我演奏这世上最美的艺术。

original: Well, I'm no bard - the far opposite of one, if that's what you're asking.
string: 嗯，我不是什么诗人——恰恰相反，如果你问的是这个。

original: It's fine. I have found an artist just as great as she was.
string: 没关系。我已经找到了一个和她一样了不起的艺术家。

original: And I'm not asking you to be one. We are each who we are... to presume otherwise brings nothing but sorrow.
string: 我也没有要求你成为那样的人。我们各自做自己就好……以为别人应该是什么样子，只会带来痛苦。

original: So, Jenassa - what's with your obsession over 'art'?
string: 那么，简拉萨——你为什么对'艺术'这么执着？

original: The world would be a colorless place without it, no?
string: 没有艺术，这世界就失去色彩了，不是吗？

original: Yeah. But from the sound of it, the only color of your art is bloody red!
string: 是啊。但听你这么说，你的艺术唯一的颜色——就是血红色吧！

original: Well, we each have our preferences. Some play their lutes... while I stick to my sword.
string: 好吧，我们各有各的喜好。有人弹鲁特琴……而我坚守我的剑。

original: But what is your art, Jordis - if you have one?
string: 那你的艺术是什么，乔蒂丝——如果你有的话？

original: Well, not singing or dancing, that's for sure.
string: 嗯，反正不是唱歌也不是跳舞，这个可以肯定。

original: You look happy, Jenassa.
string: 你看起来很幸福，简拉萨。

original: All because of your Thane.
string: 全都是因为你的武卫大人。

original: You didn't look like the type to settle down... But it suits you. Now it's as if I'm seeing my brother and Faida again, ever the joyful couple.
string: 你看起来不像那种会安定下来的人……但这很适合你。现在我仿佛又看到了我哥哥和菲达，永远那么幸福的一对。

original: Seeing people from your past, Jordis?
string: 看到了过去认识的人，乔蒂丝？

original: Yeah. You got me!
string: 是啊。被你看穿了！

original: Tell me something about your mother, Illia.
string: 跟我说说你母亲的事吧，伊雅。

original: Why? I didn't realize you cared.
string: 为什么？我不知道你居然还关心这个。

original: My own mother died to save me from the An-Xileel... Were I in your place, I could never bring myself to hurt her... Let alone kill her.
string: 我自己的母亲为了从安-希雷尔手下救我而死的……如果我是你，我绝对下不了手伤害她……更别说杀了她。

original: You were lucky to have your mother then, Jenassa.
string: 那你那时候很幸运，还能有你的母亲，简拉萨。

original: Maybe at one point, mine would've made the same sacrifice. But after years of corruption, I doubt she still loved anything besides power.
string: 也许曾经，我的母亲也愿意做出同样的牺牲。但经过这么多年的堕落，我怀疑她除了权力，已经不再爱任何东西了。

original: Was that why you struck her down?
string: 所以那就是你打倒她的原因？

original: I don't know. At that point, all I knew was that I must stop the coven and their human sacrifice.
string: 我不知道。那一刻，我只知道我必须阻止那个女巫团和他们的人祭。

original: Maybe I would've chosen differently had my mother shown a bit more warmth. But then, she wouldn't be that power-mad Hag we slew.
string: 如果我母亲曾表现出哪怕一丝温情，也许我会做出不同的选择。但那样的话——她就不会是那个我们杀死的、被权力冲昏了头的鬼婆了。

original: Tell me something about Morrowind, Jenassa.
string: 跟我说说晨风的事吧，简拉萨。

original: You'll have to be more specific with your question.
string: 你得问得再具体一点。

original: Well, specific... how?
string: 嗯，具体……怎么个具体法？

original: Morrowind is a big place. Dozens of cities, hundreds of species, with five noble houses each trying to kill the others every day.
string: 晨风是个很大的地方。几十座城市，数百个物种，五个贵族家族天天都在互相残杀。

original: I didn't know what to ask, because I knew nothing at all about the world outside the Tower. But you just gave me something to work with... Thanks.
string: 我不知道该问什么，因为塔外面的世界我什么都不知道。但你刚才给了我一些能了解的东西……谢谢。

original: Honestly, why don't you just go read a book? Surely, the witches taught you to read?
string: 说实话，你干嘛不自己去读本书呢？那些女巫总该教过你认字吧？

original: Illia - I noticed your disgust when I prayed to the Three earlier.
string: 伊雅——我注意到了，刚才我向三神祈祷时，你露出了厌恶的表情。

original: You were praying to the Daedra.
string: 你在向迪德拉祈祷。

original: Who I worship is my business. Why don't you mind your sorceries, witch?
string: 我信仰谁是我的事。你管好你的巫术就行了，女巫。

original: I was doing exactly that - until you had to bring it up.
string: 我正是在这么做——直到你非要把这事挑明。

original: Good. Then we understand each other.
string: 很好。那我们互相理解了。

original: What do you think about Wolfskull Cave?
string: 你怎么看狼头骨洞穴？

original: I think the Steward is a fool to dismiss that villager's warning - but at least, he has half the wisdom to hire professionals to investigate.
string: 我觉得总管是个蠢货，根本没把那个村民的警告当回事——但至少他还有一半脑子，知道雇专业人士来调查。

original: I just hope he pays well.
string: 我只希望他出手够大方。

original: It's not about the money for me. It's about saving people.
string: 对我来说不是钱的问题。是要救人。

original: A thousand people would fight for a thousand reasons. In the end, the only thing that matters is the job gets done.
string: 一千个人会为一千种理由而战。到头来，唯一重要的——是活儿干完了。

original: Why wouldn't the Steward pay well?
string: 总管怎么会不肯出够钱？

original: Solitude is the pearl of the north, so I don't doubt that its coffer has more than enough for two hired blades.
string: 独孤城是北方的明珠，我一点也不怀疑它的金库够付两个佣兵。

original: But the Steward sees Wolfskull Cave's rumors as a farce. That's why he didn't even care to send reinforcements.
string: 但总管把狼头骨洞穴的传闻当成一场闹剧。所以他连派援军都不上心。

original: A small pouch for our time, that's the payment he expects to afford.
string: 一小袋金币打发我们的时间——那就是他打算付的报酬。

original: With the war going on, Solitude really can't afford to investigate mere rumors.
string: 仗还在打呢，独孤城确实抽不出人去调查区区谣言。

original: Isn't that the most convenient excuse everyone uses these days.
string: 这难道不是如今每个人都用的最顺手的借口吗？

original: A farm was raided by bandits? The soldiers are off at the war camp. The city's water needs to be sanitized? The gold is all in the war chest.
string: 农场被强盗洗劫了？——士兵们都在前线营地呢。城里的水需要净化了？——金币全在军需箱里呢。

original: Maybe the Jarls are more interested in painting the map than governing their people.
string: 也许领主们更热衷于在地图上涂抹疆域，而不是好好治理他们的子民。

original: The Steward should've done more to help his people.
string: 总管本该为他的子民做更多事的。

original: The Nords are all about their honor, and nothing's more honorable than killing others on the battlefield.
string: 诺德人满嘴都是荣誉，而没有什么比在战场上杀敌更荣誉的了。

original: Where's the honor in keeping some peasants happy?
string: 让几个农民过上好日子——荣誉又在哪里？

original: Let's go.
string: 走吧。

original: Either way, the Steward's thoughts are of little consequence to us. We'll just keep doing what we always do best.
string: 不管怎样，总管怎么想对我们来说无关紧要。我们只管继续做我们最擅长的事。

original: Falk Firebeard doesn't seem like a warmonger to me.
string: “火胡”佛可在我眼里不像个好战分子。

original: Yet those around him are all sounding the war drums. Even if the Steward wanted to care, the warmongers wouldn't have permitted him.
string: 可围着他的人全都在敲战鼓。就算总管想关心——好战分子也不会允许他。

original: Enough with your cynicism. I'll hear no more of it.
string: 够了，你的愤世嫉俗我听够了。

original: Maybe don't ask for my thoughts next time, then.
string: 那你下次就别问我的看法。

original: And you care about the peasants?
string: 那你在乎那些农民吗？

original: Obviously no. I merely made an observation after spending decades on this land.
string: 显然不在乎。我只不过在这片土地上待了几十年，随口说了一句观察罢了。

original: They're all short-sighted fools.
string: 全都是目光短浅的蠢货。

original: If they see any further beyond the glory at hand, it would be a betrayal of their proud heritage, no?
string: 要是他们能看到眼前的荣耀之外的东西——那岂不是背叛了他们引以为傲的传统，你说是不是？

original: What do you think about Solitude's lighthouse?
string: 你怎么看独孤城的灯塔那件事？

original: You mean the Argonian pirate's 'proposition'.
string: 你是说那个阿尔贡海盗的'提议'吧。

original: I don't know why you're even considering to entertain him. If I know pirates, they're never going to share their spoil.
string: 我不明白你为什么还在考虑跟他周旋。以我对海盗的了解——他们绝不会把战利品分给别人。

original: Besides - should an East Empire Company vessel be wrecked after this, the situation with my debt will become most... peculiar.
string: 再说——万一之后有一艘东帝国公司的船沉了，我那笔债的事就会变得非常……微妙。

original: Besides - should an East Empire Company vessel be wrecked after this, then we'll earn the ire of Cyrodiil's greatest power.
string: 再说——要是之后有东帝国公司的船在这里遇难——那我们就会招来希罗帝尔最强大的势力的怒火。

original: I may no longer be chained to them, but their eyes are always present in Haafingar. Many more like me are still at their disposal.
string: 我或许已经不再被他们拴着了，但在海芬加领，他们的眼线无处不在。还有很多像我一样的人——仍然受他们支配。

original: The Legion may fight honorably... but the Company does not.
string: 军团也许会光明正大地战斗……但公司不会。

original: Besides - should an East Empire Company vessel be wrecked after this, then we'll earn the ire of Cyrodiil's greatest power.
string: 再说——要是之后有东帝国公司的船在这里遇难——那我们就会招来希罗帝尔最强大的势力的怒火。

original: The Legion may fight honorably... but the Company does not.
string: 军团也许会光明正大地战斗……但公司不会。

original: Don't worry, I'll ignore the Argonian pirate.
string: 放心吧，我不会理那个阿尔贡海盗的。

original: Your wisdom is greater than you realized.
string: 你的智慧比你自己以为的还要大。

original: I'm interested to see this through.
string: 我想把这件事看到底。

original: That pirate is a fool. All he spouts is rot.
string: 那个海盗就是个蠢货。从他那张嘴里吐不出象牙。

original: Well. Now that you mention it... What kind of criminal would recruit an accomplice on the street?
string: 好吧。既然你提到了……什么罪犯会在大街上招募同伙？

original: Only the foolish or the careless, I'd imagine - and neither make for good schemers.
string: 我想只有傻子或者粗心鬼才干得出来——而这两样人都成不了好的阴谋家。

original: There are riches awaiting us in this job. We just have to go and grab it.
string: 这活儿里有财宝等着我们。去拿就是了。

original: There will come a day your curiosity leads us to safe havens and good fortune, but I see that day is still far away.
string: 总有一天，你的好奇心会带我们去到安全的避风港和好运——但在我看来，那一天还早着呢。

original: What do you think about Morthal?
string: 你怎么看莫萨尔？

original: Normally, I appreciate silence and solitude - but in Morthal, even the silence grows suffocating.
string: 通常来说，我喜欢安静和独处——但在莫萨尔，连安静都压得人喘不过气。

original: A house was burnt down and a family ruined, yet the suspect still walks freely under the sun, and the town goes about its business as usual.
string: 房子烧了，家毁了——嫌疑人却还在光天化日之下自由走动，镇上的人也照常过他们的日子。

original: It's as if that's the norm here. Still, indifferent... and dead.
string: 好像这就是这里的常态似的。死寂，冷漠……没有一点生气。

original: I intend to unravel the mystery here.
string: 我打算揭开这里的谜团。

original: Unravel the mystery, or upset the design of the forces that be?
string: 揭开谜团，还是搅乱当权者的布局？

original: Maybe we should get away while we can.
string: 也许趁还来得及，我们该走。

original: Wise caution can often be confused with cowardice.
string: 明智的谨慎常常被人误认为是懦弱。

original: In my view, there's no point saving a place that doesn't care to be saved.
string: 依我看，拯救一个不在乎自己有没有救的地方——毫无意义。

original: Let's go then. I can hardly wait to breathe freely again.
string: 那走吧。我快等不及想好好喘口气了。

original: The burnt family demands justice.
string: 那个被烧毁的家庭需要公道。

original: I see your point. It may not save a soul... but the dead will find some small comfort if we avenge them.
string: 我明白你的意思。也许救不了谁……但如果我们替他们报了仇，死者也能得到一丝安慰吧。

original: I don't know what we expect to find in this town, or what yet awaits us in the marsh.
string: 我不知道我们指望在这镇上找到什么，也不知道沼泽里还有什么在等着我们。

original: But if Death is looming over Morthal, then I say we feed it what it desires - the blood of those responsible for the terror.
string: 但如果死神正笼罩着莫萨尔——那我说，就喂给它想要的：那些对这起恐怖事件负责的人的鲜血。

original: What do you think about Raven Rock Mine's secrets?
string: 你怎么看鸦石镇矿场的秘密？

original: Knowing how the East Empire Company operates, it wouldn't surprise me that they've concealed secrets beneath the mine.
string: 以我对东帝国公司行事风格的了解，他们在矿井下面藏了秘密——我一点也不意外。

original: It exists to generate wealth for the noble houses. Everything else is expendable for that goal.
string: 这座矿场的存在就是为了给贵族家族创造财富。除此之外的一切，为了这个目标都可以牺牲。

original: For them to shut down the mine, I see two explanations - one, they stood to gain much from what lied beneath, so they kept it sealed for themselves.
string: 他们关闭矿场，我看有两个解释——第一，下面的东西能让他们大赚一笔，所以他们把它封起来留给自己。

original: And two, they stood to lose much more if they let the mine be. That means whatever they'd hidden beneath... is best left forgotten.
string: 第二，如果让矿场继续开下去，他们失去的会多得多。也就是说，不管他们藏在下面的是什么……最好就此遗忘。

original: What do you think they've hidden down there?
string: 你觉得他们下面藏了什么？

original: I doubt even the Vici themselves knew, let alone a mere sellsword they employed.
string: 我怀疑连维齐家族自己都不清楚，更别说他们雇来的卖命佣兵了。

original: I honestly don't know.
string: 老实说，我不知道。

original: If I were to entertain a guess, it'd either be a Nordic ruin, full of undead longing for flesh - or a Dwemer ruin, with their steels of death.
string: 如果非要我猜的话——要么是一座诺德遗迹，里面全是渴望血肉的亡灵——要么是一座锻莫遗迹，遍布他们那致命的钢铁。

original: The Company might not care much for things besides profit, but it still operated under the Emperor's grace.
string: 公司除了利润之外或许不关心别的——但它终究是在皇帝的恩典下运作的。

original: Should an army of undead swarm the town, the Emperor - and by extension, the Company - would have much to answer for.
string: 如果一支亡灵大军涌向城镇，皇帝——连带着公司——都难逃其咎。

original: Do you think we should leave the mine alone then?
string: 那你是觉得我们不该管这个矿场？

original: I believe we should delve deeper and see what the Company has hidden.
string: 我认为我们应该深入下去，看看公司到底藏了什么。

original: Where there are risks, there are opportunities. Whatever secret lies below, it is worth protecting to the Company.
string: 哪里有风险，哪里就有机会。不管下面藏着什么秘密——那东西值得公司如此守护。

original: That either means it can make us rich, or it can change the world.
string: 那要么意味着它能让我们发财，要么意味着它能改变世界。

original: Let's go.
string: 走吧。

original: The East Empire Company's secrets await.
string: 东帝国公司的秘密在等着我们。

original: If someone pays you to, would you ever betray your patron?
string: 如果有人出钱，你会背叛你的雇主吗？

original: I suppose this question arose from my profession.
string: 我想这个问题是冲着我的职业来的吧。

original: Who put such thoughts in you? I suppose it's that sorry failure Lydia.
string: 谁让你有这种想法的？我猜是那个可怜的废物莱迪亚吧。

original: I may work for gold, but I will never sully my art by betraying those who afforded it.
string: 我或许为金币而工作——但我绝不会用背叛来玷污我的艺术，背叛那些花钱让我施展艺术的人。

original: Learn to appreciate my art, unless you want this fear to come true... when our contract expires.
string: 学着欣赏我的艺术吧——除非你想让这个担心成真……等我们的合同到期的时候。

original: After all the time we've spent together, I thought you had started to appreciate my art. I guess I was wrong.
string: 一起经历了这么多，我以为你已经学会欣赏我的艺术了。看来是我错了。

original: I'm sorry, Jenassa. I didn't mean that.
string: 对不起，简拉萨。我不是那个意思。

original: Very well. Let's put those thoughts behind us for good.
string: 很好。那就把这些想法彻底扔到脑后吧。

original: Don't the Dunmer like treachery?
string: 丹莫不是最喜欢背信弃义吗？

original: Against enemies, not those whose coin feeds me.
string: 是对敌人——不是对那些用钱养活我的人。

original: Why don't you stay silent for a while, until you've grown a mind of your own, at least.
string: 你不如先安静一会儿——至少等你自己长了脑子再开口。

original: We'll see.
string: 走着瞧吧。

original: I guess we will.
string: 看来也只能这样了。

original: Don't bring Lydia into this.
string: 别把莱迪亚扯进来。

original: So it's your own thought, then. Very well... I see now how you truly look at me.
string: 所以，这是你自己的看法了。很好……我现在知道你真正是怎么看我的了。

original: It's not your first time escorting a historian?
string: 你不是第一次护送历史学家了吧？

original: The first time I took on such a contract, it was in another Nord ruin. I reckon it was even bigger than this one.
string: 我第一次接这种活，是在另一座诺德遗迹里。我估摸着比这座还要大。

original: Supposedly, that ruin was built above an ancient Falmer burial ground, which the Nords defiled and destroyed during their conquests.
string: 据说那座遗迹建在一处古老的古伐莫墓地上方——诺德人在征服途中把它玷污并摧毁了。

original: This historian believed the Falmer ghosts had possessed the Draugr there, and intended to prove it.
string: 那个历史学家相信伐莫的鬼魂附在了那里的尸鬼身上，打算以此证明自己的理论。

original: Was that historian an elf?
string: 那个历史学家是精灵？

original: He was a full-blooded Nord. Dressed like one, drank like one, even breathed like one.
string: 纯血的诺德人。穿得像诺德人，喝得像诺德人，连喘气都像诺德人。

original: Only thing that was different? He claimed his 28th great-grandmother was the last Falmeri princess, which made him the true heir to their legacy.
string: 唯一不一样的地方？他声称他的第28代曾祖母是最后一位伐莫公主——所以他才是伐莫遗产的真正继承人。

original: What happened in that ruin?
string: 那座遗迹里后来怎么了？

original: What happened was that he kept yapping about the ancient Falmer and their glory, how the Nords' revenge for Saarthal was too harsh, and so on.
string: 后来啊——他一直在喋喋不休地讲古老的伐莫和他们的辉煌，说什么诺德人对萨瑟尔的报复太过分了，诸如此类。

original: After a certain point, I simply stopped paying attention. He gave the ruin many more pieces of his mind, no doubt.
string: 到后来，我就干脆不听了。他肯定对那座遗迹发表了很多高论。

original: I thought you'd agree with him.
string: 我以为你会同意他的说法。

original: Because I'm an elf?
string: 就因为我是精灵？

original: We Dunmer hardly even care about our own brethren, until the circumstances drive us to band together.
string: 我们丹莫连自己的同胞都几乎不怎么放在心上——除非情况逼得我们必须团结。

original: All I can say is that the Falmer got their fate, and history is already written.
string: 我只能说——伐莫得到了他们应得的命运，而历史已经写就。

original: What a fool. The Falmer are gone, only the monsters are left.
string: 真是个蠢货。伐莫早就没了，只剩下那些怪物了。

original: My thought exactly. But why should an artist argue with her patron?
string: 我也是这么想的。不过——一个艺术家何必跟出钱的人争辩呢？

original: Did the historian get what he was looking for in the Nord ruin?
string: 那个历史学家在诺德遗迹里找到他想要的东西了吗？

string: 显然没有。里面尸鬼倒是不少……但除了一个幽魂之母和她的几十个崽子，伐莫的踪迹我们半点也没找到。

string: 他整个人都垮了，不过无所谓。我只在乎拿到我辛苦挣来的报酬。
